pages.api:
# API reference

> The readings, the report, the store vector, the export endpoints and the settings.

## Reading `transcript/<name>` (default `wake0`)

`transcript.v1`, class `reading`: the command as `text`, with the times of the transcript it came from. `confidence` is always 1.0 (not measured).

## Reading `telemetry/<name>`

`telemetry.v1`: `transcripts.seen`, `commands`, `wakes.bare`, `transcripts.ignored`, `bus.connected`.

## stdout

`{"command": "...", "from": "..."}` per command, then one report per interval:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string | `ok`, `no_source`, `simulate`, `replay` |
| `provenance` | string | `MEASURED`, `SYNTHETIC` or `REPLAY` |
| `phrase`, `listening_to` | string | |
| `transcripts_seen`, `commands`, `bare_wakes`, `ignored` | numbers | since start |
| `armed` | bool | a bare phrase is waiting for its command |
| `last_command` | string/null | |
| `bus` | object | `connected`, `subscribed`, `published`, `error` |
| `error` | string | only with `no_source` |

## Store vector (id 34)

Eight floats; a source that is absent is **-1**.

| Slot | Name |
|---|---|
| 0 | `seen` |
| 1 | `commands` |
| 2 | `bare_wakes` |
| 3 | `ignored` |
| 4 | `armed` (0 or 1) |
| 5 | `published` |
| 6 | `bus_connected` (0 or 1) |
| 7 | `command_ratio` (commands / seen) |

## Export (`http://127.0.0.1:8068`, continuous mode)

`/status`, `/raw`, `/history`, `/guide`, `/healthz`.

## Settings

`--interval`, `--window`, `--phrase`, `--listen-s`, `--source`, `--name`, `--api-bind`, `--replay`, `--simulate`.
pages.phrase:
# The phrase

> What counts as the wake phrase, and what happens after it.

## Matching

Case and punctuation are ignored. Each word of the phrase must appear in order and next to each other. A word of five letters or more may be one edit away (`arduin` for `arduino`); shorter words must be exact, so `hay arduino` is not `hey arduino`.

## After the phrase

- **Words after it** are the command: `Hey Arduino, what time is it?` publishes `what time is it`.
- **Nothing after it** arms the gate for **Armed time** (8 s by default). The next transcript, with or without the phrase, is the command. One command per arming.
- **The phrase mid-sentence** works: `well, hey arduino what time is it` publishes `what time is it`.

## Changing it

Set **Wake phrase** to any words, for example `computer`. A single common word wakes on every mention, so prefer two words.
pages.setup:
# Set up

> Run it from a shell, then place it on the node.

## From a shell

```
cog-wake-word --once --simulate                         # a canned conversation
cog-wake-word --once --replay transcripts.jsonl         # lines {"text": ..., "start_ns": ..., "end_ns": ...}
cog-wake-word                                           # continuous; gates transcript/asr0 from the broker
```

Each command is printed as `{"command": ..., "from": ...}` and, with a broker, published.

## Placed on a node

Place `wake-word` in the same project as `asr`. Its `cog.toml` declares the input `transcript` and the outputs `transcript` and `telemetry`. It declares no device and runs no model.
pages.start:
# Start here

> Act only on what is said to the board, not on everything it hears.

`wake-word` reads the transcripts of `asr` and passes on a command only when it follows the wake phrase (default **hey arduino**). It publishes the command, without the phrase, on `transcript/wake0`. An assistant cog reads that topic and never sees the chatter.

## The short path

1. **Run `audio-in` and `asr`.** → see their guides
2. **Try the gate with no hardware.** `cog-wake-word --once --simulate` runs a canned conversation: two commands out of five transcripts.
3. **Place it.** It reads `transcript/asr0` and publishes `transcript/wake0`. → see **Set up**

## How the signal flows

```diagram
flow
```

## Honest limits

- It confirms on the transcript, so a command costs one full recognition first. The brick spike found that the on-device keyword model alone fires on ordinary speech; this is the second stage that makes it safe, and it needs no NPU time.
- Wake detection is as good as the recognizer: a phrase heard as something else is a missed wake.
- It is not a speaker check. Anyone's voice, or a speaker playing a recording, wakes it.
pages.troubleshoot:
# Troubleshoot

> What each failure looks like and what to do.

## `no_source`

`no broker: WEFTOS_COGBUS is not set` when run from a shell without a broker; otherwise `bus.error` has the broker's refusal (`unauthorized` or `unknown_topic` means the cog was placed without its `[[inputs]]`).

## It never wakes

Read `transcripts_seen`. Zero: `asr` publishes nothing (check its guide) or the **Transcript source** does not match its **Name**. Many but no commands: look at `asr`'s `last_text`; the recognizer may hear the phrase differently. Use `--once --replay` with a file of what it heard to see the gate's verdict.

## It wakes on talk that was not for it

The phrase is too common. Use two words, or a rarer one.

## The command is missing its first words

Speech after a pause longer than `asr`'s hangover is a second utterance. Say the phrase and the command together, or rely on the armed window (a bare phrase, then the command).
